description: The index of every SKILL.md in this repo, and the only place a skill's byte budget lives. `scripts/check-load.mjs` reads it: a skill on disk with no row is a finding, a row without a `trigger` or `when` is a finding, two rows sharing their first three trigger words are a finding, and a skill past its `budget_bytes` is a finding. `ideal_bytes` is the convergence target and never fails - the gap between it and `budget_bytes` is debt a later pass pays down. `phase` is the lifecycle step a skill owns (0-7), null when it spans the lifecycle; `family` separates the workflow set from the audit set. `supersedes` names the block of the deleted project-workflow instruction that moved here, so a reviewer can prove nothing was dropped.

skills.trigger: the lifecycle end to end: which phase comes next, what it produces, its exit gate
supersedes: copilot-instructions#The lifecycle (the two rules that cost epics)
skills.when: Before starting any phase, and whenever the next step is unclear.

skills.trigger: scoping an epic: the binding text, re-measuring an amendment's premises, the deferral record
skills.when: At an epic's start, before the business requirements and before any code.

skills.trigger: writing an epic's business requirements: the README, one story file per story, AC and status
skills.when: After the epic's scope is agreed, before design and before code.

skills.trigger: the design gate: the component set per surface, each component's state list, the human preview
skills.when: Before writing the first TSX of a surface. The human preview gate sits here.

skills.trigger: building one story: the pre-implementation checks, the change checklist, Tier 1, the commit gate
skills.when: While implementing one story, from the first edit to the commit.

skills.trigger: closing a story: boxing the AC, the BR/IMP pair, the doc-code truth-check, status and date
skills.when: When the story's code is committed and its acceptance criteria are met.

skills.trigger: closing an epic: the Phase 5 surface table by name, Tier 2, the docs audit, the carry-forward
skills.when: When the epic's last story is closed and the epic is ready to ship.
supersedes: copilot-instructions#The lifecycle (phase 5 row and its surface list)

skills.trigger: shipping an epic as one pull request: the PR template, gate evidence, CI green
skills.when: When the epic is closed and its work is ready for review as one pull request.

skills.trigger: archiving closed epics in a deferred batch: which folders move, the archive exemptions
skills.when: In a deferred batch after shipping, never mid-epic.

skills.trigger: Tier 1 gates: the five commands every code change runs, and what each counts
skills.when: Before every commit, and while working to see whether a change is still clean.
supersedes: project-workflow#Quality gates (the single-source rule and the Tier 1 table)
project-workflow#Quality gates (the build-is-the-typecheck, npm-test and Gate-1-fast-path notes)

skills.trigger: Tier 2 gates: the pre-merge and close gates, what each counts, and when a red result is debt
skills.when: Before a merge, a story close or an epic close.
supersedes: project-workflow#Quality gates (Notes that cost a run when missed)

skills.trigger: adding a quality gate: the row, the npm script, the solar command, the parity checks
skills.when: When a new check needs to be enforceable, before writing it.

skills.trigger: auditing backend code: error message format, module boundaries, service layer
skills.when: Run before closing a backend story.

skills.trigger: auditing documentation and verification artefacts against the code they describe
skills.when: Run at an epic close, or on any doc a code change invalidated.

skills.trigger: auditing frontend code, UIUX fundamentals and the AI-slop checklist
skills.when: Run after a frontend feature and before closing a UI story.

routing: A description opens with the moment, not the subject: 'closing a story:', not 'stories'. The router matches task wording, so the words a person would use to start the task lead.

One namespace prefix per family, and no other skill may use it: 'Phase N of the lifecycle:', 'Tier N quality gates:', 'Run this skill when auditing X'. A prefix is a claim of exclusivity, so a second skill with the same prefix is a routing defect.
A skill that owns a lifecycle phase carries the phase number in both the description and `phase`. Two sources for one fact is the drift this registry exists to prevent.
The trigger is what the skill does; `when` is the moment it fires. Neither may restate the other, and no two rows may share their first three words - if they do, the router cannot tell them apart.
